CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Mayor  www.SanMarinoCA.gov
Tony Chou, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Hunter Chang, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

John Chou, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Calvin Lo, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  FRIDAY, OCTOBER 31, 2025 AT 8:30 AM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council with valuable
information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically, adjourned
meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City
Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626) 300-0705 48 hours prior to the
meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the meeting will
proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will do it’s best to resolve
any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:
Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00 p.m. the day before
the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will be distributed to City Council during the
meeting. Any comments received after 3:00 p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not
provided to City Council at the meeting.

AGENDA – OCTOBER 31, 2025  PAGE 1 of 8
 Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module during the
meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted after the in-person comments. Written Zoom
comments will be read or summarized, then printed and made part of the public record for the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chang, Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Vice Mayor Chou, and
Mayor Shepherd Romey

POSTING OF AGENDA

The special meeting agenda is posted 24 hours prior to each special meeting at the
following locations: City Hall, 2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890
Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The special meeting
agenda is also posted on the City’s website: http://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

  NEW BUSINESS

 1.  APPROVE THE REGULATORY TRAFFIC CONTROL CHANGES AS
  OUTLINED IN THE REPORT; ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. R-25-31: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN MARINO,
  CALIFORNIA, DESIGNATING SELECT INTERSECTIONS AS STOP
  INTERSECTIONS AND AUTHORIZING THE INSTALLATION OF STOP
  SIGNS”; ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. R-25-33: “A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN MARINO, CALIFORNIA,
  AUTHORIZING THE INSTALLATION OF “NO RIGHT TURN ON RED”
  SIGNS WITH SCHOOL-RELATED TIME RESTRICTIONS AT SELECT
  INTERSECTIONS ALONG HUNTINGTON DRIVE”; ADOPT RESOLUTION
  NO. R-25-34: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  SAN MARINO, CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING REDUCED SPEED LIMITS
  IN DESIGNATED SCHOOL ZONES “WHEN CHILDREN ARE PRESENT”;
  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. R-25-35: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN MARINO, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING

AGENDA – OCTOBER 31, 2025  PAGE 2 of 8
   THE INSTALLATION OF APPROXIMATELY EIGHTY (80) FEET OF RED
  CURB (NO PARKING ZONE) ALONG THE WEST SIDE OF SAN MARINO
  AVENUE SOUTH OF HUNTINGTON DRIVE”; APPROVE PROCUREMENT
  OF NINE (9) SOLAR-POWERED SPEED RADAR DRIVER FEEDBACK
  SYSTEMS FROM TAPCO IN THE AMOUNT OF $72,026.03

  Recommendation: Staff recommend the City Council 1) approve the regulatory traffic
  control changes as outlined in the report, 2) adopt Resolution No. R-25-31: “A
  resolution of the City Council of the City of San Marino, California, designating select
  intersections as stop intersections and authorizing the installation of “Stop” signs,” 3)
  adopt Resolution No. R-25-33: “A resolution of the City Council of the City of San
  Marino, California, authorizing the installation of “No Right Turn on Red” signs with
  school-related time restrictions at select intersections along Huntington Drive,” 4)
  adopt Resolution No. R-25-34: “A resolution of the City Council of the City of San
  Marino, California, establishing reduced speed limits in designated school zones when
  children are present,” 5) adopt Resolution No. R-25-35: “A resolution of the City
  Council of the City of San Marino, California, authorizing the installation of
  approximately eighty (80) feet of red curb (No Parking Zone) along the west side of
  San Marino Avenue south of Huntington Drive,” and 6) approve the procurement of
  nine (9) solar-powered speed radar driver feedback systems from Tapco in the
  amount of $72,026.03. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to 1) approve the regulatory traffic control changes as outlined in the report,
  2) adopt Resolution No. R-25-31: “A resolution of the City Council of the City of San
  Marino, California, designating select intersections as stop intersections and
  authorizing the installation of “Stop” signs,” 3) adopt Resolution No. R-25-33: “A
  resolution of the City Council of the City of San Marino, California, authorizing the
  installation of “No Right Turn on Red” signs with school-related time restrictions at
  select intersections along Huntington Drive,” 4) adopt Resolution No. R-25-34: “A
  resolution of the City Council of the City of San Marino, California, establishing
  reduced speed limits in designated school zones when children are present,” 5) adopt
  Resolution No. R-25-35: “A resolution of the City Council of the City of San Marino,
  California, authorizing the installation of approximately eighty (80) feet of red curb
  (No Parking Zone) along the west side of San Marino Avenue south of Huntington
  Drive,” and 6) approve the procurement of nine (9) solar-powered speed radar driver
  feedback systems from Tapco in the amount of $72,026.03.”

 2.  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN MARINO AND ALL CITY
  MANAGEMENT SERVICES, INC. FOR CROSSING GUARD SERVICES IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $236,522.56

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the agreement for crossing
  guard services provided by All City Management Services Inc. If the City Council
  concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the Agreement between the City of San Marino and All City
  Management Services, Inc. for crossing guard services beginning July 1, 2025, and
  ending June 30, 2026.”

 3.  APPROVAL TO WAIVE THE SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT COST FOR THE

AGENDA – OCTOBER 31, 2025  PAGE 3 of 8
   SAN MARINO HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING PARADE IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $5,095.50

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council waive the costs associated
  with the special event permit for the San Marino High School Homecoming Parade. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, then the appropriate motion
  would be:

  “I move to waive the costs associated with the special event permit for the San
  Marino High School Homecoming Parade totaling $5,095.50.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

 4.  FIND THE ROOF REPAIR PROJECT EXEMPT UNDER THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA); APPROVE A PUBLIC WORKS
  AGREEMENT WITH S&T CONTRACTORS SERVICES, INC. IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $264,976.20 FOR WINDSTORM-RELATED ROOF REPAIRS
  TO CITY FACILITIES; AND AUTHORIZE THE PARKS AND PUBLIC
  WORKS DIRECTOR/CITY ENGINEER TO APPROVE CONTINGENCIES IN
  AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $26,497 WITH ALL COSTS TO BE PAID
  BY THE CALIFORNIA JOINT POWERS INSURANCE AUTHORITY

  Recommendation: Staff recommend that the City Council 1) find the project
  categorically exempt under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), 2)
  approve a Public Works Agreement with S&T Contractors Services, Inc. in the amount
  of $264,976.20 for roof repairs at Lacy Park and City Hall and 3) authorize the Parks
  and Public Works Director/City Engineer to approve contract change orders and other
  contingencies in an amount not to exceed $26,497, with all costs to be paid by the
  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority as outlined in the agreement. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to (1) find the project categorically exempt under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Sections 15301(d) and 15302(c) of
  Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations (Class 1 Existing Facilities
  Exemption), (2) approve a Public Works Agreement with S&T Contractors Services,
  Inc. in the amount of $264,976.20 for windstorm-related roof repairs to City
  facilities, and (3) authorize the Parks and Public Works Director/City Engineer to
  approve contract change orders and other contingencies in an amount not to exceed
  $26,497, with all costs to be paid by the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority
  as outlined in the agreement.”

 5.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A CONTRACT WITH LANCE, SOLL, &
  LUNGHARD, LLP, FOR AUDIT SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEARS 2025-26
  THROUGH 2027-28, WITH TWO ONE-YEAR RENEWAL OPTIONS IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $129, 100

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council award a three-year auditing
  services contract to Lance, Soll, & Lunghard (LSL), LLP. If the City Council concurs

AGENDA – OCTOBER 31, 2025  PAGE 4 of 8
   with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I (1) move to award a three-year professional services agreement in the amount of
  $129,100 to LSL, LLP for auditing services; (2) authorize the City Manager to execute
  the agreement on behalf of the City; and (3) authorize the City Manager to execute
  the renewal options of the agreement.”

 6.  APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE AGREEMENT WITH EIDE
  BAILLY, LLP TO INCREASE NOT-TO- EXCEED AMOUNT TO $50,000

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve amendment No. 1 to the
  agreement with Eide Bailly, LLP. If City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation
  an appropriate motion would be:

  ”I move to approve Amendment No, 1 to the agreement with Eide Bailly, LLP and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment.”

 7.  REQUEST FOR AUTHORIZATION TO USE THE COOPERATIVE
  AGREEMENT WITH LONG BEACH BMW FOR THE GRANT FUNDED
  PURCHASE OF NEW 2024 BMW R 1250 RT-P POLICE MOTORCYCLE, IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $33,967.66

  Recommendation: Staff recommend that the City Council authorize the use of the
  Cooperative Agreement with Long Beach BMW, approve the purchase of one new
  police motorcycle, and authorize staff to proceed with the purchase in the amount of
  $33,967.66. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to approve the purchase of one new police motorcycle in the amount not to
  exceed $33,967.66.”

 8.  APPROVAL OF 3-YEAR AGREEMENTS WITH ROCKETOLOGY, BRIT
  WEST SOCCER, AND PAYKE GYMNASTICS, AND APPROVAL OF 2-YEAR
  AGREEMENT WITH LENEAR SPORTS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve of: 1) the three-year
  contract with Rocketology (Professor Egghead), 2) the three-year contract with Brit
  West Soccer, 3) the three-year contract with Payke Gymnastics, 4) the two-year
  contract with Lenear Sports (Skyhawks Sports), and 5) waive bidding for these
  services. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to approve of: 1) the three-year contract with Rocketology (Professor
  Egghead), 2) the three-year contract with Brit West Soccer, 3) the three-year
  contract with Payke Gymnastics, 4) the two-year contract with Lenear Sports
  (Skyhawks Sports), and 5) waive bidding for these services.”

 9.  APPROVAL OF OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY (OTS) GRANT AGREEMENT
  FOR SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (STEP) FOR
  $48,000

AGENDA – OCTOBER 31, 2025  PAGE 5 of 8
   Recommendation: Staff recommends City Council approve the agreement for OTS
  Grant Funding and authorize the Operations Division Police Commander and the
  Finance Director to enter into the agreements with the Office of Traffic Safety in an
  amount not to exceed $48,000 in the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026, and approve
  FY 2025-26 budget appropriations as noted in the Staff Report. If the City Council
  concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve and authorize the Operations Division Police Commander and the
  Finance Director to enter into the agreements with the Office of Traffic Safety in an
  amount not to exceed $48,000 in the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026, and approve
  the FY 2025-26 budget appropriations as noted in the staff report.”

 10. APPROVAL OF FY 2024-25 BUDGET CARRYOVERS AND FY2025-26
  RE-BUDGETS AND FINAL FY 2024-25 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the requested FY 2024-
  2025 carryovers, updates to the FY 2025-2026 re-budgets, and the budget
  amendments to FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the requested FY 2024-2025 carryovers, updates to the FY
  2025-2026 re-budgets, and the budget amendments to the funds and accounts as
  noted in the attachments and the Staff Report.”

 11. COMMITMENT OF DONATIONS FUND YEAR-END BALANCE RESERVES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the
  accompanying resolution to commit the balance as of June 30, 2025, as noted in the
  attachments. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-25-29 to commit the balance of $342,895 in the
  Donations Fund as of June 30, 2025.”

 12. APPROVAL OF A FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND
  RESTATED  CITY MANAGER  EMPLOYMENT  AGREEMENT  AND
  CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-25-32 TO REVISE THE
  SALARY SCHEDULE

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve a First Amendment to
  the Amended and Restated City Manager Employment Agreement and adopt
  Resolution No. R-25-32, amending the salary schedule. If the City Council agrees,
  an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated City
  Manager Employment Agreement Between the City of San Marino and Philippe
  Eskandar and to Adopt Resolution No. R-25-32.”

AGENDA – OCTOBER 31, 2025  PAGE 6 of 8
  13. APPROVAL OF CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY CLOSURE CALENDAR FOR
  2026

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve of the Crowell Public
  Library closure calendar for 2026. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the Crowell Public Library closure calendar for 2026.”

 14. FALL 2025 PUBLIC TREE REMOVAL LIST

  Recommendation: This is an informational item. Therefore, no action is required by
  City Council.

 15. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF SEPTEMBER
  2025

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of
  September 2025.”

 16. RECEIVE AND FILE  MONTHLY  DISBURSEMENTS  REPORTS  FOR
  SEPTEMBER 2025

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of September 2025. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of
  September”

 17. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the September 2025
  Minutes. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to approve the Minutes of the Special Meeting of September 10, 2025, the
  Regular Meeting of September 10, 2025, and the Adjourned Regular Meeting of
  September 26, 2025.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San

 Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

  ALISON WALKER
Posted: 10/24/2025
  CITY CLERK
